title: Dhow Boat Tours
tagline: See the coast from the water.
shortDescription: Explore Somalia’s historic shoreline aboard traditional handcrafted wooden dhow vessels.

story.whatItIs: A guided coastal voyage aboard a traditional Somali dhow — the same handcrafted wooden vessels that have carried merchants, fishermen, and travelers along the Horn of Africa for centuries.
story.whereItHappens: Departing from working harbors like Bosaso, dhow tours trace the shoreline past coral-stone forts, fishing fleets, and open pelagic waters.
story.whatToExpect: Calm-water sailing, close encounters with resident dolphin pods, and conversation with the dhow builders and crews who keep this maritime heritage alive.

gallery.caption: Traditional dhow under sail off the Bosaso coastline.
Bosaso harbor, home port for coastal dhow voyages.
Resident dolphin pods often accompany dhow crossings.

highlights: Sail aboard a handcrafted wooden dhow
Pass historic coral-stone fortifications
Meet artisan dhow builders and maritime crews
Frequent dolphin sightings along the route
conservationThemes: Supports traditional dhow builders and heritage maritime craft
Zero-wake, low-speed boating near coastal wildlife
Pack-in, pack-out — no waste left on the water

title: Coral Garden Snorkeling
shortDescription: Snorkel above intact coral reefs teeming with parrotfish, rays, and vibrant biodiversity.

story.whatItIs: A shallow-water snorkeling excursion over some of the Western Indian Ocean’s most intact coral gardens.
story.whereItHappens: The sheltered lagoons and outer reef flats of the Bajuni Atolls, with calm, high-visibility water for much of the season.
story.whatToExpect: Reef-top swims among branching and table coral, giant clams, and reef fish, guided by local snorkel leaders trained in reef-safe practices.

gallery.caption: Snorkeler above a shallow coral garden in the Bajuni Atolls.
Branching and table coral formations near the reef crest.
The sheltered lagoons of the Jubaland archipelago.

highlights: Shallow, calm-water reef access
Guided by reef-safe snorkel leaders
Giant clams and reef fish at arm’s length
Beginner-friendly, no certification required
conservationThemes: No-touch reef etiquette to protect fragile coral polyps
Reef-safe sunscreen required for all participants
Proceeds support the Bajuni Barrier Reef Resilience research program

title: Deep Pelagic Diving
shortDescription: Scuba dive into largely unexplored Somali reef drop-offs where oceanic giants congregate.

story.whatItIs: A multi-day scuba expedition into deep reef walls and pelagic drop-offs, designed for certified divers seeking largely unsurveyed waters.
story.whereItHappens: The Guardafui Deep off the tip of the Horn of Africa, where the Somali Current upwelling draws nutrient-rich water — and the animals that follow it — close to shore.
story.whatToExpect: Wall dives beside whale sharks and oceanic manta rays, with dive briefings led alongside Blue Ocean’s marine research teams.

gallery.caption: Divers along a pelagic drop-off in the Guardafui Channel.
Whale sharks feeding in the seasonal upwelling zone.
The Hafun Peninsula, gateway to the deep pelagic shelf.

highlights: Wall dives on unsurveyed reef drop-offs
Seasonal whale shark and manta ray encounters
Dive briefings informed by active research data
For certified advanced divers only
conservationThemes: No-touch, no-chase interaction guidelines with pelagic megafauna
Dive data contributes to the Bari Coast Whale Shark Tagging Study
Certified dive operators only, with mandatory buoyancy checks over reef

title: Artisanal Pelagic Fishing
tagline: Experience the traditions of the coast.
shortDescription: Experience traditional sustainable fishing on the Indian Ocean alongside veteran fishermen.

story.whatItIs: A day on the water with Somali artisanal fishermen, learning traditional handline and hoop-trap techniques passed down for generations.
story.whereItHappens: The productive pelagic shelf off Bargaal, where seasonal upwellings bring yellowfin tuna and other pelagic fish within reach of small boats.
story.whatToExpect: Hands-on handline fishing, a shoreline catch, and firsthand insight into the fishing cooperatives that anchor Somalia’s coastal economy.

gallery.caption: Yellowfin tuna landed using traditional handline methods.
Fishing dhows departing at dawn from Bargaal.

Guided by veteran Somali fishing cooperatives
Fresh shoreline catch and coastal cuisine
Insight into sustainable artisanal fishing methods
conservationThemes: Traditional handline and hoop-trap methods that avoid seafloor damage and bycatch
Respect for seasonal closed periods protecting breeding stock
Supports Fair Trade Handline Certification for Somali artisanal fleets

title: Bajuni Island Odyssey
tagline: Find the islands beyond the shore.
shortDescription: Visit remote uninhabited islands and turquoise lagoons off Somalia’s southern border.

story.whatItIs: A multi-day expedition by boat through the Bajuni Archipelago’s chain of coral islands, islets, and hidden lagoons.
story.whereItHappens: The southern Jubaland coast, from Kismayo’s harbor down toward the remote reaches near Ras Kamboni.
story.whatToExpect: Island hopping by traditional outrigger and dhow, remote beach landings, and time with the seafaring Bajuni community who have navigated these reef passages for centuries.

gallery.caption: Remote coral islands of the Bajuni Archipelago.
Sea turtles nesting on undisturbed island beaches.
Sheltered seagrass lagoons between the islands.

highlights: Multi-day boat expedition through remote atolls
Time with the seafaring Bajuni community
Untouched white-sand beach landings
High chance of dugong and sea turtle sightings
conservationThemes: No-anchor zones over seagrass meadows and coral heads
Supports Bajuni Archipelago Dugong Drone Survey research
Respect for community-managed island territorial waters

title: Dolphin & Whale Watching
shortDescription: Witness hundreds of acrobatic spinner dolphins and migrating humpback whales in pristine waters.

story.whatItIs: A guided boat excursion to observe resident dolphin pods and, in season, migrating humpback whales.
story.whereItHappens: The Gulf of Aden corridor off Puntland, a resting and migration route for cetaceans crossing the Arabian Sea.
story.whatToExpect: Engine-idle observation of spinner dolphin pods riding the bow wake, and — during the winter migration window — distant humpback breaches and tail slaps.

gallery.caption: Spinner dolphins riding the bow wake in the Gulf of Aden.
Humpback whales breaching off the Bari coastal cliffs.
Deep coastal waters along the migration corridor.

highlights: Resident spinner dolphin pods
Seasonal humpback whale migration
Engine-idle, no-chase observation protocol
Guided by marine mammal researchers
conservationThemes: Respectful-distance protocols to avoid disturbing pods
Supports the Maritime Route Whale Collision Advisory System
No-chase, engine-idle observation guidelines for all vessels

title: Underwater Photography Expedition
shortDescription: Guided underwater and aerial expeditions capturing Somalia’s best-kept marine frontier.

story.whatItIs: A guided expedition for underwater and coastal photographers, pairing camera time with marine research fieldwork.
story.whereItHappens: A rotating circuit across Somalia’s richest reef and coastline subjects, from Bajuni coral gardens to Qandala’s black coral drop-offs.
story.whatToExpect: Structured shoots at reef sites and cleaning stations, with guidance on light, buoyancy, and approach — and the option to contribute images to Blue Ocean’s species photo-ID archives.

gallery.caption: Coral garden photography subjects in the Bajuni Archipelago.

title: Coastal Cliff Safari
tagline: Walk the edge of the continent.
shortDescription: Discover dramatic volcanic limestone cliffs, hidden ocean coves, and pristine white sands.

story.whatItIs: A multi-day trek along Somalia’s dramatic limestone headlands, tracing coastline that few visitors have walked.
story.whereItHappens: The Karkaar mountain ridges of the Bari coast, where cliffs plunge directly into the Gulf of Aden.
story.whatToExpect: Clifftop trails, hidden coves accessible only on foot, and sweeping views over deep pelagic waters where whales and dolphins are often visible from shore.

gallery.caption: Karkaar limestone cliffs meeting the Gulf of Aden.
Coastal bluffs near Qandala along the trekking route.
Hidden coves accessible only by clifftop trail.

highlights: Multi-day clifftop and canyon trekking
Hidden coves reachable only on foot
Whale and dolphin sightings from shore
Karkaar Ridge volcanic limestone geology
conservationThemes: Stay-on-trail practices to protect nesting seabird colonies
Pack-in, pack-out waste policy on all treks
Local guide partnerships support community-based coastal stewardship
